name: ysymyth/ReAct
why: A1 reference prompts and HotpotQA/ALFWorld code; frozen since 2024 (read-only). Lesson to borrow: 1-2 in-context trajectories were enough, and A1's failure table (repeat loops, empty search results) is the checklist for a loop detector

name: noahshinn/reflexion
why: A2 code incl. LeetcodeHardGym; reflect-on-failure loop with a 1-experience memory. Lesson: the loop helped where a real test/oracle existed (A4, A5), so wire reflection to executed tests, never to self-opinion

name: princeton-nlp/tree-of-thought-llm
why: A3 code with all prompts; 5.5k completion tokens per Game-of-24 case. Lesson: search is for tasks the base model fails; log tokens per case next to success before adopting

name: billxbf/ReWOO
why: A7 code: planner/worker/solver split with #E variables. Lesson: plan-first cuts tokens ~5x on QA but needs a re-plan path when the environment is unknown (A8)

name: sierra-research/tau-bench
why: A9 benchmark: simulated user + DB-state grader + pass^k reliability metric. README warns its tasks are outdated and points to tau2-bench; lesson: version benchmarks and re-check graders. Borrow pass^k and end-state grading

name: sierra-research/tau2-bench
why: Successor to A9 with fixed airline/retail tasks and new domains; shows a benchmark needs ongoing task fixes. Lesson: grade by final database state and run k trials per task in the kit's benchmark

name: lm-sys/RouteLLM
why: A12 router framework with per-request cost threshold and a calibrate_threshold script. Lesson: calibrate the threshold on your own traffic; A12 Table 2 shows routers trained out of distribution perform near random

name: xiaowu0162/LongMemEval
why: A13 benchmark and memory-pipeline code (index/retrieve/read). README notes a 2025-09 cleaned dataset after history sessions interfered with answers; lesson: benchmark data needs a changelog and contamination check

name: TheAgentCompany/TheAgentCompany
why: A14 self-hosted company environment with checkpoint graders, simulated colleagues and OpenHands baselines. Borrow checkpoint-based partial credit plus a strict all-checkpoints success metric for the kit's app tasks

name: microsoft/autogen
why: Archived by Microsoft (README: no fixes, research-only, migrate to Agent Framework); holds A11 Magentic-One (python/packages/autogen-magentic-one) and agbench. Lesson: a research orchestration framework was retired, so pin versions and keep the kit's orchestration thin; read agbench for repetition/isolation controls

name: langchain-ai/langgraph
why: Stateful graph orchestration with durable execution (resume after failure), human-in-the-loop interrupts and memory. Lesson: persist agent state outside the context window, as the kit's progress files do; read, do not adopt a framework

name: anthropics/claude-cookbooks
why: patterns/agents/ holds minimal notebooks for A15's patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer. Borrow the minimal-implementation style and the latency/budget multi-agent notebook

name: letta-ai/letta
why: MemGPT successor; README says current source moved to letta-code, a coding-agent harness with terminal UI and server. Lesson: the memory-agent line ended up inside a coding harness; compare its memory handling with the kit's file-based notes

name: openai/swarm
why: Experimental/educational handoff-and-routines library, now marked replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK. Lesson: handoffs as plain function returns are enough to prototype; the production path added guardrails, sessions and tracing

name: openai/openai-agents-python
why: Production successor to Swarm: agents-as-tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing. Lesson: built-in tracing and guardrails were the additions after the educational prototype

name: mem0ai/mem0
why: Memory layer for agents; its README self-reports LoCoMo 92.5 and LongMemEval 94.4 (vendor numbers, not independent). Lesson: test any memory service on A13 yourself before relying on it

name: princeton-pli/hal-harness
why: Archived harness for cost-controlled, parallel, reproducible agent evaluation (HAL) with Weave cost logging; README says work moved to agent reliability. Lesson from A10: report cost with accuracy; borrow its one CLI across benchmarks idea

name: harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2
why: A24 task set (89 hard CLI tasks, each with instruction, Dockerfile, tests, oracle solution); model for the kit's own task format (unverified: repo contents not read, downloaded code is untrusted)

name: jennyzzt/dgm
why: A22 reference code for the Darwin Godel Machine (self-modifying coding agent with an archive of agents); study how it sandboxes self-modification and what the objective-hacking guard looks like

name: xingyaoww/code-act
why: A20 CodeAct reference code and CodeActInstruct data; frozen since 2024-05, the live descendant is OpenHands (already in 04)

name: uiuc-kang-lab/agentic-benchmarks
why: A18 Agentic Benchmark Checklist (ABC) materials; usable as a pre-flight checklist for the kit's own benchmark tasks; no detected license, so read only

name: google-deepmind/alphaevolve_results
why: A25 results repository (discovered programs and verification notebooks) from AlphaEvolve; shows what an automated-evaluator loop produces and how outputs are checked

name: algorithmicsuperintelligence/openevolve
why: Open-source reimplementation of the AlphaEvolve loop (A25): LLM mutates code, programmatic evaluator scores it; a pattern for the kit's evaluator-gated improvement loops
